title: Threadsmith: field notes and impact hypotheses
content:
Overview:

Short: synthesis of 8 customer conversations (May–Jun 2026) focused on runtime flakiness, cost surprises, and feature asks that would meaningfully reduce manual mitigation work for CS/SE teams. This is a working doc (notes + hypotheses + quick win proposals).

Context and sample customers: 
- FinAssist (mid-market SaaS, heavy chat + mem retrieval) — worried about token-cost spikes when model falls back to larger variants during long contexts.
- LegalVault (enterprise, private deploy) — needs deterministic routing to model variants for compliance reviews; observed model mismatch after rollouts.
- Searchly (startup, vector-heavy) — sending dense embedding pipelines with duplicate items and paying multiply; wants dedupe at API or SDK layer.
- RetailOps (large customer) — intermittent latency spikes tied to KV-cache misses and multi-tenant contention.

Common themes (synthesized):
1) Invisible fallbacks and cost surprises
   - Customers do not see when a request routes to a cheaper/compatible "fallback" model vs the primary model. When fallback picks a larger model (eg during cold-start rollouts) some saw 2–5x token cost in periods.
   - Quote: "We saw a sudden bill leap — traces showed the model ID changed mid-day but no alert. Felt like a silent upgrade." — FinAssist eng lead.
2) KV-cache observability and cold-start signals
   - SRE and platform owners need a signal for the % of requests hitting KV-cache vs first-token generation. Without it, troubleshooting latency regressions is manual.
   - Requests with long prefix distributions (chat histories) amplify the impact of cold KV misses.
3) Embedding dedupe and batching guidance
   - High-volume embedding pipelines contain frequent duplicate inputs (re-ingestion, incremental backfills). Customers want an API-side dedupe hint or a best-practice SDK plugin.
   - Small startups cannot afford moderate over-ingestion; they ask for a low-friction toggle (dedupe=true) that would apply a short-term cache keyed by content hash.
4) Model mismatch during rollouts / no effective canary telemetry
   - Customers doing canary comparisons need per-request model-version annotation, deterministic routing, and easy A/B result capture.
5) Lack of per-request unit-cost estimate + predicted latency
   - CS calls: customers repeatedly ask for a per-request estimated cost and latency before sending big batches. This avoids surprise charges.

Impact Hypotheses (ranked):
- High impact, low complexity (fast wins):
  * Per-request model-version header in responses (explicit header + logging field). Benefit: immediate reduction in investigation time for CS and customers. Effort: low (runtime + response header).
  * KV-cache hit-rate metrics per route/model surfaced in Console (percent hitting cache, 1m/5m windows). Benefit: reduces SRE debugging time and ties to latency-slo alerts. Effort: medium (metrics + UI row).
  * Embedding dedupe toggle prototype (SDK + server flag) that caches short-lived content-hash with TTL 1h. Benefit: cost savings for ingestion-heavy customers. Effort: low–medium.
- Medium impact, medium complexity:
  * Per-request estimated cost preview in SDK (local estimate based on tokens + model profile) with opt-in telemetry to improve accuracy. Benefit: lower surprise bills. Effort: medium (model profiles + SDK UX).
  * Canary telemetry and structured A/B capture: enable customers to tag routes as canary and automatically capture paired responses for rollout evaluation. Benefit: safer rollouts and faster rollback decisions. Effort: medium–high (data capture + storage + flip controls).
- High impact, higher complexity:
  * Smart fallback reporting + alerting: when routing policy changes model class for >X% of requests, emit an alert + visible incident timeline in Console. Benefit: prevents silent cost regressions. Effort: high (routing observability, policy hooks).

Quick sketches / proposals: 
- "Model-ID" response header + tracing tag (implementation notes):
  * Expose: X-Redwood-Model-Id, X-Redwood-Model-Variant, X-Redwood-Routed-By (policy id).
  * Record in traces and console logs.
  * Backfill: query logs for last 30d in support tool.

- "KV Cache Panel" in Console:
  * Tiles: cache-hit-rate, avg first-token-latency, tail p95/p99 latency, and correlation to request size distribution.
  * Quick filter: route, model-variant, org or customer id.

- Embedding dedupe MVP:
  * Server flag: embed_dedupe=ttl:3600 (content-hash keying). SDK convenience: dedupe=true on batch embeddings.
  * Safety: opt-in only, limit dedupe cache entries per org. Telemetry: counter for deduped items and tokens saved.

Open questions & risks (recorded in-calls):
- Privacy: dedupe cache needs to avoid storing raw customer content persistently. We should store only content-hash + TTL, and ensure KMS policies for private deployments.
- Consistency: dedupe might change inference semantics if customer expects repeated embeddings to be retried (edge-case: transient upstream corrections). Needs customer education and opt-in.
- Billing model: how to reflect deduped requests in usage reports (we should surface tokens saved as a metric).

Actionable next steps (owner, ETA):
- Implement Model-ID header (owner: eng-serving-runtime — Evan Singh). ETA: prototype by 2026-07-15.
- Add KV-cache metrics to per-route telemetry (owner: observability — Marisol). ETA: initial roll by 2026-08-01.
- Prototype embedding dedupe flag with SDK hook (owner: developer-experience — Liam Park). ETA: POC by 2026-07-30.
- Run 3-week pilot with FinAssist, Searchly, LegalVault to validate dedupe and Model-ID header. (owner: customer-success — Priya). ETA: mid-August.

Notes-to-self / CS playbook snippets (for immediate use):
- When customer reports cost spike: ask for request logs and check X-Redwood-Model-Id once header is available. If not available, request last-activity logs + trace ids.
- For latency spikes: correlate avg prefix length and KV-cache-hit-rate per route. If hit-rate < 60% during spike window, escalate to infra SRE.
- For embedding cost concerns: check for repeated content-hashes in ingestion windows; suggest batching + dedupe SDK workaround.

Appendix — representative verbatim customer lines (anonymized):
- "We want to know if the model changed — even a header would be fine." — FinAssist
- "Can you give us a signal that our chat requests are missing cache? We end up throwing the kitchen sink at optimization blind." — RetailOps platform lead
- "A simple dedupe toggle would save us thousands in reingestion loops." — Searchly founder

End / version notes: 0.1 (draft). Will iterate post pilot.
